question: As printed (not as recorded): binary classification of MCI vs healthy controls in ADNI from T1 structural MRI. The task, population class and channel are the same. The record's 96.81% for P-109 is its three-class AD/MCI/HC accuracy, which is a different contrast, so it was replaced by P-109's binary MCI/HC figure (condition 6).
metric: Accuracy with accuracy (P-125 80.00% subject-level vs P-109 94.23% slice-level); AUC with AUC also available (85.71-90.31% vs 97.15%).

figures.P-125: 37 MCI/37 HC, 60/40 subject split (about 30 test subjects): mean test accuracy 80.00% (RF/ANN), Wilson (24/30): 0.627-0.905. The abstract gives 82.14%. Test AUC up to 90.31%.
figures.P-109: BrainViT-L, MCI/HC: accuracy 94.23%, AUC 97.15%. 370 MCI + 315 HC (685 subjects) from a 1075-subject ADNI set; about 50 slices per subject (16,280 MCI + 17,732 HC slices); random 90/10 slice split. No interval reported. Wilson on subjects (n=685): 0.922-0.957; on test slices (about 3,400): 0.934-0.950; on about 69 subjects (if 10% of subjects): 0.861-0.977.

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists. P-109 reports no subject-level split and no morphometric-feature model; P-125 reports no slice-based model. P-109's other models on the same slices (ResNet50 85.13% up to BrainViT-B 93.12%) share P-109's design, not P-125's.
performance_validity: Borderline for P-109. Its MCI/HC AUC of 97.15% (and 98.05% three-class, 98.52% AD/HC) meets the 0.97 threshold on internal validation with no external cohort. The cohort (685 subjects in the contrast) is not small, so the Section 3.5 exclusion is not met on its letter. However, the test set is a random 10% of slices from the same subjects as the training slices, so there is no subject-independent evaluation, and Section 3.5 names the split unit as a design that inflates reported accuracy. Whether the exclusion extends to a large cohort evaluated this way is the operator's call. P-125 is not flagged.

candidate_explanations.difference: Split unit: random slice-level split, so slices of one subject can sit in both training and test sets (P-109), vs a subject-level hold-out (P-125).
candidate_explanations.quote: The images were shuffled randomly, and all experiments were carried out by splitting the data into 10 % for testing and 90 % for training.

candidate_explanations.difference: Input representation and unit of evaluation: about 50 2D slices per subject classified individually vs 8 amygdala scalars per subject.
candidate_explanations.quote: used for training were V, VN, DC, and TR for both hemispheres of the amygdala, for a total of 8 features.

candidate_explanations.difference: Sample size: 685 subjects in the contrast vs 74.
candidate_explanations.quote: A total of 1075 individuals, including 390 with AD, 370 with MCI, and 315 HC, were used to create a balanced dataset for the 2D model.

candidate_explanations.difference: Architecture: a CNN-transformer hybrid on images vs classical classifiers on hand-crafted features.
candidate_explanations.quote: 97.13 % with 98.52 % AUC for AD/HC and 94.23 % with 97.15 % for MCI/HC classifications

reason: On the figures printed for the shared question (binary MCI vs HC in ADNI, structural MRI), P-109's 94.23% and P-125's 80.00% lie outside each other's intervals, and no matched figure reconciles them. The pair is borderline on condition 5 only. P-109's MCI/HC AUC of 97.15% comes from internal validation with no external cohort, on a random 90/10 split of about 34,000 slices drawn from the same 685 subjects. The subject count is not small, so the exclusion is not met on its letter, but the evaluation has no subject-independent test set, which is the concern behind the exclusion. If the exclusion is read to cover this design, the pair fails condition 5; if not, it qualifies, with the slice-level split as the leading candidate explanation (not shown to be sufficient).

quotes.quote: The images were shuffled randomly, and all experiments were carried out by splitting the data into 10 % for testing and 90 % for training.
A total of 1075 individuals, including 390 with AD, 370 with MCI, and 315 HC, were used to create a balanced dataset for the 2D model.
97.13 % with 98.52 % AUC for AD/HC and 94.23 % with 97.15 % for MCI/HC classifications
BrainViT-L 20.1 4.6 97.13 98.52 94.23 97.15 (Table 4 row: params, FLOPs, AD/HC ACC, AUC, MCI/HC ACC, AUC; cells joined)
used for training were V, VN, DC, and TR for both hemispheres of the amygdala, for a total of 8 features.
The mean test accuracy was 80.00 ± 2.43 %, 79.29 ± 5.78 %, 77.86 ± 3.71 % and 80.00 ± 3.97 % for the RF, SVM, KNN and ANN models respectively.
